newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian PM to present government by end-Friday.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian PM to present government by end-Friday.

text.p: Slovenia, the most economically advanced of the former Yugoslav republics, should have a new government by the end of Friday.

Prime minister- designate Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats is expected to present his new cabinet later in the day after talks with other parties dragged on late into Thursday night.

"The government list with the names of at least 10 out of 15 ministers and the explanations for their nominations has to be presented to parliament by midnight," Matjaz Kozelj, a parliamentary president spokesman told Reuters.

Under the constitution, Drnovsek had 15 days to form a new government after he won a mandate from parliament by a single vote last week with support from several smaller parties, including the former communist party.
A Liberal Democrat spokeswoman said a final decision would most probably be reached at the party's council meeting which was scheduled to start at around 5 p.m. (1600 GMT).

Drnovsek, whose party took 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats in an inconclusive November general election, needs the backing of at least one of the three rightwing parties of the so-called "Spring" alliance to form a majority administration.
The alliance, which together holds 44 seats, comprises the conservative People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats.
Drnovsek offered seven to nine cabinet posts to the group, but the alliance on Monday rejected the proposal and told him to go back to the drawing board.
No agreement has yet been reached although analysts said the proposal was favourable to the "Spring" parties.
"All options still seem to be open. We may get a government in which all parties will be included, or one with a majority of one vote only," a political analyst said on Friday.
The new government will be the third since Slovenia's independence in 1991. Drnovsek has been prime minister since April 1992.
